slug: 2026-06-02 SIN, ST Digital to deploy cloud services at Lomé data center

facts.fact: Connecting Africa reports that the state-owned SIN operates the Lomé Data Centre, where SIN and ST Digital are launching private cloud services, with SIN's director saying firms can rent half or full racks for data hosting; date is the article's, as it gives no opening date.
Connecting Africa describes the SIN-operated Lomé Data Centre as a Tier III-certified facility, without naming the certifying body; date is the article's.

note: carried from datacentres; no document opened

facts.fact: ST Digital and SIN signed a partnership at Lomé on 26 May 2026 to deploy a private-cloud catalogue at the Lomé Data Centre, operated by SIN, to be sold to businesses and organisations.
SIN and ST Digital state that the SIN-operated Lomé Data Centre is Tier 3 certified with a 99.982% SLA; operator statement, certifying body not named.

note: carried from datacentres; no document opened

facts.fact: RFI reports Togo put Lomé Data Centre into service in May 2021, offered to companies, chiefly telecom operators, to host their servers and buy services from other customers on site, managed by Africa Data Centres for five years.

note: carried from datacentres; no document opened

facts.fact: ST DIGITAL says it officially launched its colocation offering in Lomé on 15 October 2025, letting companies host their own servers in a data centre in Lomé (facility not named; operator ST DIGITAL).
facts.system: ST DIGITAL colocation data centre, Lomé

facts.fact: ST DIGITAL states the data centre in Lomé hosting its new colocation offering is Tier III (operator statement; no certifier named, facility not named).

facts.fact: The Lomé Data Centre's own home page, published 24 September 2025, describes a carrier-neutral facility in operation offering racks, cages, suites, disaster recovery, interconnection and managed services, with 1+ MW critical power and a 99.982% availability SLA.
The Lomé Data Centre's operator describes it as Togo's first Tier III+ facility (operator statement; no certifier named), per its home page dated 24 September 2025.

facts.fact: DatacenterDynamics reports Lomé Data Center, Togo's first carrier-neutral data center, was inaugurated in the week of the article (published 2021-06-08), with 400 sqm for the private sector, operated by Africa Data Centres.

note: carried from datacentres; no document opened

facts.fact: Togo First reports Lomé Data Centre was inaugurated on 4 June 2021, providing colocation server hosting to private operators, managed and operated by Africa Data Centres.

note: carried from datacentres; no document opened

facts.fact: President Gnassingbé inaugurated Lomé Data Centre on 4 June 2021, a facility hosting servers for several companies on a colocation basis, with 400 sq m of private and 100 sq m of government server halls; owned by SIN.

note: carried from datacentres; no document opened

facts.fact: ST DIGITAL, a pan-African operator of sovereign data centres serving banks, telcos, administrations and enterprises, says it has infrastructure deployed in Togo among seven countries; facility not named, and as_of is the post date as none is given.

ST DIGITAL states its data centres across its seven countries, Togo included, are Tier 3/TIA-942 constructed; the claim is fleet-wide, no Togo facility is named, and as_of is the post date as none is given.

facts.fact: ST Digital launched cloudstore.africa in Lomé on 17 October 2024, hosting business data on local servers (VPS) in Togo, run in the government-invested data centre its CEO calls the right one; the centre is not named in the document.

note: carried from datacentres; no document opened

facts.fact: The Council of Ministers communiqué of 21 December 2022 states that a data centre built by the state's digital infrastructure company (SIN) in Lomé is operating and offers storage services to economic operators, and authorises its transfer to a private operator not yet named; the document gives no opening date, so the date is that of the council meeting.
